$description: What the system can grow into, written by the lead on 16 November 2026. 'now' is on the branch v2-direction and checked by a tool; 'next' has its inputs ready and could start this week; 'later' needs a decision or something that does not exist yet. Sources for the component order: the handoff doc's ranked list (build files per component in the app as of 14 November) and what version 0.2 of this repo already built and tested.

lanes.why: Every other lane reads from here.

items.name: Colour roles, light and dark
items.detail: 171 roles, snapshot proved exact, 734 pairs audited, none failing with the 77 fixes applied.

items.name: Type, radius, spacing, density
items.detail: 74 tokens generated as they stand in Figma; naming breaks the standard and is listed, not renamed.

items.name: Border width, focus ring, control and icon size, motion, elevation, scrim
items.detail: 22 tokens proposed in the repo because the five components cannot be built without them. To add in Figma.

items.name: Descriptions for all 308 tokens
items.detail: The standard's rule 9, and what agents read through the Figma connector. A script can draft them from the name; a person confirms.

items.name: Renames the standard asks for
items.detail: Radius by size not height, type roles without 'small' and 'base', collection names, Tailwind's own prefixes for type. One breaking release, with aliases kept for one version.

items.name: Increased-contrast theme
items.detail: A third mode on the colour collection. The audit tool can target 7 to 1 by changing one number.

items.name: Letter spacing, mono font, layer order, opacity, breakpoints
items.detail: Not started anywhere. Each needs one design decision first.

items.name: Gradients: keep or move to Sandbox
items.detail: 63 variables no component uses. The standard itself suggests moving them.

items.name: Prune unused roles
items.detail: 86 of the 171 colour roles are used by no starred Figma component. Keep only what a screen needs.

lanes.why: Ordered by how many files in the app use each one.

items.name: Button
items.detail: 235 files in the app.

items.name: DropdownMenu
items.detail: 83 files. Covers the model selector's needs: groups, radio and checkbox items.

items.name: Dialog
items.detail: 49 files plus about 20 modal wrappers.

items.name: Input
items.detail: 26 files plus the password field. Label, description and error are parts of it.

items.name: Tabs
items.detail: 24 files.

items.name: Spinner, Sheet, Avatar, Chip
items.detail: 19, 16, 15 and 11 files. Their Figma colour is already 76 to 100 percent on semantic tokens.

items.name: Tooltip, Badge
items.detail: 87 and 70 files, but half their Figma colour still comes from the old HeroUI theme. Specs can be written now; Figma needs rebinding.

items.name: Switch, Checkbox, Toast
items.detail: 13, 9 and 3 files. Checkbox exists in version 0.2 of this repo, tested, without a framework.

items.name: AlertDialog, Popover, Select, RadioGroup, Textarea
items.detail: Each is a Radix primitive with a published keyboard pattern, so a spec is mostly transcription.

items.name: Table, DatePicker, Combobox, Accordion, Breadcrumbs, Card
items.detail: In Figma today, bound to older collections. Decide which stay.

lanes.why: What the app has and no Figma component covers. A pattern is an arrangement of components, with its own spec.

items.name: Composer (chat input)
items.detail: Six of the open UI fixes are here. Built from Input, Button and DropdownMenu.

items.name: Model selector
items.detail: Four open fixes. A DropdownMenu with group labels and radio items; the spec's example already has that shape.

items.name: Chat message, proposal card, status line
items.detail: Built and tested in version 0.2 on the old token names. To re-point at the new tokens.

items.name: Sidebar and its items
items.detail: The active state needs design first.

items.name: Skeleton, Divider
items.detail: 30 and 13 files, no Figma component.

items.name: Checkout: cost summary, error summary
items.detail: Built and tested in version 0.2. They belong in a commerce layer, apart from the core.

lanes.why: One name, written once in Figma, generated everywhere else.

items.name: Figma snapshot with checksum proof
items.detail: An agent runs a read-only script; a checker proves the copy exact.

items.name: Token build: DTCG files, CSS variables, Tailwind theme, tokens.json
items.detail: Deterministic; two runs are identical.

items.name: Contrast audit, naming lint, Figma-to-code diff
items.detail: Each proves itself on planted faults.

items.name: Specs to stylesheet, typed props, docs and state map
items.detail: Generated from the spec with no model in the loop.

items.name: Gallery and browser tests from the spec
items.detail: State map, keyboard, axe, contrast, target size, focus ring, pictures.

items.name: Storybook
items.detail: The handoff asks for it. The examples are plain modules, so stories can be generated from them; not installed here.

items.name: Code Connect
items.detail: Links each Figma component to its React file. Needs the Components file and the Radix renames in Figma.

items.name: Scheduled snapshot and a pull request when Figma changes
items.detail: The diff tool already names every change; an agent opens the pull request and never merges it.

items.name: Round trip: spec back into Figma, then diff
items.detail: Nathan Curtis's test of whether a spec carries everything. Needs write access to a sandbox Figma file.

items.name: Pictures compared with Figma
items.detail: Each example beside its Figma frame. Needs the Components file.

items.name: Changesets and a generated changelog
items.detail: The standard asks for it; needs the package's home to be decided.

lanes.why: People and agents build from the same source.

items.name: tokens.json with names, values, CSS names and reasons
items.detail: JSON, which the standard prefers to prose for agents.

items.name: Specs as JSON, with every requirement naming its check
items.detail: An agent can read what must hold and which test proves it.

items.name: Short AGENTS.md for the new package
items.detail: Under 60 lines, pointing at the standard, the tokens and the specs. The repo's current AGENTS.md describes version 0.2.

items.name: llms.txt and a docs index
items.detail: Generated from the specs and tokens.

items.name: The four skills: ds-token, ds-component, ds-review, ds-migrate
items.detail: Named in the standard. The tools on this branch are their checks.

items.name: Agent test on the new package
items.detail: Version 0.2 was tested by giving a fresh agent only the docs. The same test, on these five components.

items.name: MCP server over tokens and specs
items.detail: So an agent asks for one component's contract and loads nothing else.

lanes.why: The spec is the contract; each platform maps roles to its own controls.

items.name: React with Radix
items.detail: What the app's engineers ship.

items.name: Plain CSS on data attributes
items.detail: The generated stylesheets need no framework and no Tailwind.

items.name: Tailwind v4 theme
items.detail: Generated; not yet compiled with Tailwind here.

items.name: Plain HTML without JavaScript
items.detail: Version 0.2 proved a checkout that pays with scripts off. Button and Input work as plain HTML with the same stylesheet; Tabs, DropdownMenu and Dialog need native fallbacks.

items.name: Web components for the other frameworks
items.detail: UI SDK was measured in version 0.2: 15 to 63 kilobytes a part. Worth it for a date picker, not for a button.

items.name: iOS and Android
items.detail: The role list says what each control must do; nothing is built.

lanes.why: Every check on this branch is a machine's. None of it shows the system works for people.

items.name: Screen reader pass on the five components
items.detail: VoiceOver and NVDA. The tests assert attributes, not what is heard.

items.name: A real phone
items.detail: Touch targets, the on-screen keyboard, iOS zoom.

items.name: Is pink too close to the error red?
items.detail: The measurements say the two are about 25 degrees of hue apart. Five people, one task, would settle it.

items.name: Engineers build one real screen from the package
items.detail: The handoff's own goal for the week.
